title: Field extension does not increase the dimension of a locally finite type scheme
statement: Let $k,K$ be fields and let $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ specify a field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $a:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] satisfies $\dim(X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K)\le\dim X$, where dimension is topological Krull dimension with empty-space value $-\infty$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. No quasi-compactness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: For an affine open U = Spec A of X, local finite type of a makes A a finite type k-algebra. The pullback of U to Spec K is Spec(A tensor_k K). The affine field-extension dimension theorem, with the symmetry of the tensor factors, gives dim(U_K) = dim(U). This includes A = 0 and the empty affine open.

source.place: Tag 00P3, lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension, globalized by affine opens; existing proof: lean/WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/FieldBaseChangeDimension.lean, topologicalKrullDim_pullback_le_of_field, lines 61-79

proof.text: The pullbacks of all affine opens of X form an open cover of X_K. Every such open has dimension dim(U) <= dim(X), by the preceding step and monotonicity for an open subspace. Apply the dimension bound for an open cover to conclude dim(X_K) <= dim(X). If X_K is empty, the same argument gives bottom <= dim(X); no nonemptiness or quasi-compactness is used. This is the complete argument of the existing topologicalKrullDim_pullback_le_of_field proof, so no new Lean statement is introduced.
